newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures end mixed in narrow trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures end mixed in narrow trade.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled mixed Friday amid weaker cash prices on forecasts of milder weather next week and a Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) price cut for Monday peak offers.
Many active contracts were locked in a 30 cent range. Most of the business was concentrated in 1997 summer deliveries.

April California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled up one cent at $11.88 a megawatt hour (MWh) after bouncing between $11.75 and $11.95. May COB ended unchanged at $10.85. Other COB contracts finished flat to 25 cent lower.
April Palo Verde (PV) futures settled unchanged at $15.77 after moving in a 20 cent range. May PV ended down three cent at $15.17. Active PV months finished four to 20 cents higher.

There was little fresh fundamental news to drive the electricity complex, while many traders and brokers were absent because they were attending a Western Systems Power Pool (WSPP) conference being held in Los Angeles.
The remaining participants kept a close watch on the plant outages in the western U.S. and next week's weather outlook.
The 750 megawatt (MW) unit 5 at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in New Mexico will be down for at least another week and possibly three more weeks, the operator said.
Moreover, output from the plant's 750 MW unit 4 has been cut to 415 MW due to mechanical problems, with no timeline yet set for a return to full power.
A 750 MW unit at the Navajo power plant near Page, Ariz., the 1,221 MW Palo Verde 3 and 1,080 MW San Onofre 2 nuclear power units remained out of service.
Readings in the Northwest were expected to run four to eight degrees below normal into the weekend, and then warm to three to six degrees above normal by early next week
In the Southwest, a strong southerly air flow is expected to keep the region's day readings running four to eight degrees above normal through Tuesday.
BPA lowered its firm peak power prices for Monday by 25 cents to $15.50/MWh for Northwest sales and $16.50 for California-Oregon Border (COB) sales.
Firm, peak COB electricity for Monday fell to $16.50-17.00 from Thursday's $17.00-18.00, while firm, peak PV power for Monday tightened to $19.50-20.50 from $18.00-22.00 Thursday.
Market sources anticipated the complex would fall next week when participants return from the WSPP meeting.
"People are going back to fundamentals and they are bearish. It won't be as hot in the Southwest and it won't be as cool in the Northwest. Load should be coming off," said one Northwest trader.
NYMEX estimated 182 COB and 463 PV contracts were sold compared with Thursday's 267 COB and 295 PV lots.
